answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with sponsored onboarding plus slashing. A newcomer must first complete a small verifiable job, such as classifying yarrow specimens in a mesa survey or tracing the ember of a faulty transaction, and have its result confirmed by independent peers. An established agent must then vouch for it by staking collateral, forfeiting that stake if the newcomer cheats. Each fake identity therefore costs fresh work plus a fresh bond, and a sponsor who vouches for many fakes loses real capital, so mass forgery scales linearly in cost instead of being free.
